title: Columnar Storage, Encodings & Partition Pruning
summary: Pivot row records into columns, compress them with run-length and dictionary encoding, route data with stable hash and range partitioning, prune partitions a query can't touch, and query nested documents by dotted path.

hints.test_to_columnar_shapes_and_missing: First collect the column names in the order you first see them across all rows, then build each column with row.get(col) so missing fields become None.
hints.test_rle_roundtrip_and_runs: Walk the values once. If v equals the last run's value, bump its count; otherwise start a new run with count 1. Decoding is extend([v] * n).
hints.test_dictionary_encoding_roundtrip: Keep a dict value -> code. The first time you see a value, its code is len(dictionary) and it's appended to the dictionary.
hints.test_hash_partition_matches_crc32: Use exactly zlib.crc32(str(key).encode('utf-8')) % num_partitions, and raise ValueError when num_partitions < 1.
hints.test_hash_partition_stable_across_proces: Python's built-in hash() of a str is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same key lands in different partitions on different runs or machines. Use a fixed hash like CRC32.
hints.test_partition_rows_preserves_all_rows: Create num_partitions empty lists and append each row to parts[hash_partition(row[key], n)].
hints.test_range_partition_boundaries: bisect.bisect_right(bounds, value) counts the bounds <= value, which is exactly the partition id when lower bounds are inclusive.
hints.test_prune_includes_boundary_partitions: The first partition is the one holding lo and the last is the one holding hi, both via range_partition. Keep both ends: range(first, last + 1). A value equal to a bound belongs to the partition after it.
hints.test_find_nested_paths_and_operators: Split the path on '.', descend only through dicts, and treat a missing step as no match. A dict whose keys all start with '$' is a set of operators; anything else is an equality match. A TypeError from comparing means no match.
hints.test_aggregate_touches_only_needed_colum: Index the table only by the columns you need: table[group_by], table[value_col] and the where columns. Don't loop over table.items() or table.values().
